heroHeadline: Afghan Taliban Orders TTP Out of Kabul Then Denies It; Op Ghazab lil-Haq Enters Day 73 With No Ceasefire
heroSubtitle: On May 8, 2026 (Day 72), RFE/RL reported that the Afghan Taliban leadership ordered TTP (Fitna al-Khawarij) commanders to relocate from Kabul to south of the capital — the most concrete action visible to outside observers following the April Urumqi talks. Two anonymous TTP members confirmed the order. Hours later, a senior Afghan Taliban official called the report 'baseless' and 'Pakistan's mind games,' maintaining the Taliban's longstanding public denial of any TTP presence on Afghan soil. On Day 73 (May 9), the conflict's diplomatic impasse deepened: no formal ceasefire has been signed, no Urumqi Round 2 date has been set, China has remained publicly silent since the May 5 Dangam civilian strike, and Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq remains officially active. The structural contradiction at the core of the stalemate is now fully exposed — any Taliban compliance with Pakistan's Urumqi demands would require publicly acknowledging TTP's Afghan presence, which the Taliban refuses to do. UN OCHA reports 160,000+ Afghans facing acute food insecurity in conflict-affected eastern provinces, and Pakistan's mass deportation campaign has expelled 146,000+ undocumented Afghans in 2026 alone.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
